title: The red balloon race
text:
On Saturday there was a fair in Dewi's village. There were games, music and a big stall that sold sweet corn. Dewi and her little brother Bima went with their grandmother.

At the fair, a man was giving out balloons. "Choose one," he said. Dewi chose a red balloon and Bima chose a yellow one. They tied the strings to their wrists.

"Let's have a race," said Bima. "The first one to the corn stall wins."

They ran as fast as they could. The balloons bounced above their heads. Bima was quicker, but just before the stall his string slipped off his wrist. The yellow balloon floated up into the sky.

Bima stopped. His eyes filled with tears. "My balloon!" he cried.

Dewi looked at her red balloon. Then she looked at her brother. She slowly untied her string and held it out. "You can share mine," she said. "We can hold it together."

Bima wiped his eyes and smiled. They walked to the stall together, holding the red balloon between them. Grandmother bought two cobs of sweet corn, and nobody minded who had won.
